guitar.guitaristsText: Jonny Greenwood / Ed O'Brien / Thom Yorke
guitar.evidence: Jonny Greenwood's Telecaster Plus and Ed O'Brien's Stratocasters/Jazzmasters are well documented among Radiohead gear-heads.

tone.target: jangly clean-to-crunch with roomy post-rock shimmer
tone.profile: jangly clean-to-crunch with roomy post-rock shimmer
tone.summary: A chimey, chorus-enhanced signal chain using a Fender-style clean amp (US Deluxe) paired with a bright cab, emphasizing clarity and space for post-rock textures.

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Slightly lift the signal for better definition and attack.
blocks.gap: Using Boost instead of a dedicated EQ to maintain clean headroom while adding subtle punch.

blocks.purpose: Achieve the required 'chorus-like width' without sounding overly wet or distracting.
Provide the 'slight breakup on strums' and clean attack without heavy distortion.
blocks.gap: Green OD is chosen over Blues OD for a slightly more vintage, chimey grit that complements the Tele/Strat vibe.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the clean, bright Fender/Vox tone required for the verses.
Provide a bright, articulate sound suitable for clean arpeggios and jangly tones.
Add the 'roomy post-rock shimmer' and sense of space.
Implement the 'drop dotted-eighth delay' effect for rhythmic texture.
blocks.gap: The GP-180 does not have a dedicated dotted eighth setting, so manual time adjustment is used to approximate the desired rhythm.

blocks.purpose: Enhance the 'bright upper mids' and overall clarity while keeping the tone open.

improvements.summary: Upgrade IR for increased realism and room depth.

proposals.reason: Enhance the spacious, post-rock shimmer required by 'Karma Police'.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased depth and natural room tone.
